Luc: Heads-up from a customer session: when they reorder deep stacks the item sometimes 'teleports' two slots past where you drop it. They called it 'ghost jump'. Attached short vid. Harper: I can repro. Dragging index 18 to index 12 will occasionally end up at index 9 after a tiny pause. Looks like our placeholder/virtualization boundary math + immediate sim trigger. Sofia: UX proposal: introduce a short "settle" period (100-150ms) after drop before committing to server so the list can finish animating. Also show a very subtle ghost placeholder animation rather than instant swap so people keep spatial context. Raja: Backend note: sim infra will sometimes return 202/204 while warming. Frontend treats anything !=200 as failure right now, which causes the red toast flip mid-edit. We should accept 202 as accepted-processing and show a small inline subtle state (dot or dim) rather than a full error. @DevOpsBot can we log which sim requests return 202 for the next 24h? DevOpsBot: Logged: sim-ack-status stream enabled for routing-editor for next 24h. Creating temp metric sim.ack.202.count. a11y-bot: Automated audit: drag handle contrast low (2.8:1). Interactive area 18px (fail). Recommendations: increase target to >=44px, ensure focus-visible ring meets contrast, expose move controls to keyboard users, and add an aria-live update with the moved position. Harper: Keyboard flow thoughts: add explicit Move menu (on focus press M to open) with options Move Up/Move Down/Jump to Top/Jump to Bottom and show hotkeys. That avoids relying solely on Space/Enter drag emulation which is flaky with virtualization. When a move completes announce: 'Moved rule "Block-Proxy" to position 7 of 22'. Sofia: Microcopy tweaks: the current toast 'Invalid rule precedence' is unhelpful. Suggest full message: 'Order not applied 14 check for locked rules or circular dependencies in this policy.' Short toast: 'Order not saved 14 resolve dependencies.' Also add a link on the toast to open the dependency inspector. Luc: I like the "settle" idea. Also important: should live simulation run while the user is dragging? My vote: suspend simulation live-runs during reorder gestures (call it "preview suspension") and trigger a single reconciliation when the user drops/commits. Less noise and fewer spurious failures. Raja: Agreed. Plan: (1) treat 202 as processing, show subtle spinner near Preview title; (2) suspend sim during active drag/keyboard move and resume on commit; (3) add 120ms settle before saving; (4) expose keyboard Move menu and an aria-live string. I'll open the backend/client PRs. Harper: For the microinteraction can we try a 90ms crossfade + 110ms translate so it feels anchored but not heavy. Also lower the snap slab width near virtualization seams to avoid crossing chunks. Sofia: Example aria-live snippet for the pattern library:
Moved rule "Block-Proxy" to position 7 of 22
And a short keyboard help text: 'Focus row, press M to open move menu (Up/Down/Home/End).' a11y-bot: Adding checklist item: role="button" + aria-label on handle, hit target >=44px, focus-visible outline >=3:1, add aria-live announcements, provide keyboard-only move controls and document hotkeys in help overlay. Luc: Next steps: @Raja will do client change for 202 handling + preview suspension + settle debounce, @Sofia will update toast copy + add dependency inspector link, @Harper will mock the crossfade/translate and new small placeholder animation, and I'll make a small regression test that runs a deep-reorder scenario and asserts no toast-flip. Sync Tuesday 10am PT if anyone wants to QA. Raja: I'll also add a temporary metric to track how often the client sees 202 during reorder flows so we can verify the fix reduced bad UX. Sofia: I'll draft the copy PR and add the link target to the inspector ticket. Thanks team. :sparkles: Harper: Thanks! Putting the short vid and a quick Loom in the ticket. :camera:
